status_meaning: Complete means the bounded interaction below is implemented, not that an entire unit or all possible exercises are complete. Independent review status is separate.

rows.implemented: Synthetic model assumptions, fixed parameters and experimental limits are explicit.
rows.limit: Selected contexts, not a general modelling course.

rows.topic: Data display, location, dispersion, skew and outliers
rows.implemented: Sample values and an outlier example support other labs.
rows.limit: No dedicated histogram-with-unequal-width, boxplot, skewness or data-summary workbench.

rows.implemented: Transparent weighted draws and distinct replacement/nonreplacement designs.
rows.limit: General conditional probability and conditional-independence scenarios absent.

rows.implemented: Drag/keyboard/numeric pairs; Pearson, fitted y-on-x, prediction, outlier, extrapolation and zero-correlation counterexample.
rows.limit: Bounded synthetic data, no real-data upload; descriptive inference conditions remain separate.

rows.implemented: Weighted finite moments and Binomial/Poisson PMFs are calculated.
rows.limit: No general PMF/CDF editor or complete discrete-uniform lesson.

rows.implemented: Normal density, signed tails, quantiles and stated Normal models.
rows.limit: No general arbitrary-event Normal calculator or source-population simulator.

rows.implemented: Exact null laws and test tails; Binomial(3,p) GOF example.
rows.limit: Moments/approximation comparison and continuity correction UI absent.

rows.implemented: Not built.
rows.limit: No continuous PDF/CDF manipulation, area or quantile lesson.

rows.topic: Continuous uniform; Normal approximation and continuity correction
rows.implemented: Not built.
rows.limit: No event-specific continuity-correction interaction.

rows.implemented: Fixed card model and12 distinct finite-frame identities; census example at n12.
rows.limit: Bounded illustrative designs, not a complete survey-frame or advantages/disadvantages course.

rows.implemented: Fixed model→original sample→one statistic→repeated distribution, with original-case recall; census in finite-frame lab.
rows.limit: Two explicitly different sampling models. No full sampling-frame survey toolkit.

rows.topic: Hypotheses, critical regions, tails and discrete tests
rows.implemented: Binomial and Poisson H0 laws, chosen H1/alpha, inclusive integer regions and observed decisions.
rows.limit: Bounded display n≤200, Poisson lambda≤30; tails can be evaluated outside the shown PMF window.

rows.implemented: Distinct variable IDs, explicit model conditions, signed means, squared variance terms, sign-flip comparison and point mass.
rows.limit: Two variables; no covariance/related-variable model. Repeated IDs are rejected.

rows.topic: Random, stratified, systematic and quota sampling
rows.implemented: Same12 identities under four explicit mechanisms; population weights, missing strata and ordering comparison.
rows.limit: Bounded finite frame; systematic n divides12. One deterministic convenience mechanism does not represent all quota implementations.

rows.implemented: Rule versus realised estimate; mean/first/mean+2/variance rules; separate n/R, expectation/finite simulation, weighted exact cases.
rows.limit: Finite-variance IID with replacement in the card lab; n1 sample variance unavailable.

rows.implemented: Weighted discrete-source means, expectation/SE and analytic Normal mean references.
rows.limit: No original Normal source-population experiment; approximation conditions remain explicit.

rows.implemented: Known-sigma repeated intervals, confidence changes, fixed-parameter interpretation; mean UI also has stated large-sample estimated-s intervals.
rows.limit: Non-Normal small-n coverage approximate; estimated-s repeated reference fixes the plug-in s and does not resample its estimation.

rows.implemented: One-mean z, known variance, chosen tails and null-reference decision with stated conditions.
rows.limit: No small-sample Student t fallback. Synthetic summaries are an illustrative model.

rows.implemented: Skewed finite-variance populations, raw/standardised mean views, independent n/R, SE and explicit approximation conditions.
rows.limit: No universal n30 guarantee; discrete source pools only. Unknown-sigma route requires explicit large-sample justification.

rows.implemented: Difference of means, variance addition, known-sigma and stated large-sample estimated-s z routes.
rows.limit: Independent groups only; no paired design or Welch t interface.

rows.implemented: Uniform/specified four-class probabilities and Binomial(3,p), original-data edits, E/contributions, meaningful pooling, fitted parameter accounting where supported.
rows.limit: Normal/Poisson/continuous-uniform GOF absent. Fitted Binomial inference uses only the original four unpooled classes. fit=true with any actual pooling is unsupported in either operation order: p/decision/referenceDF withheld, even if E≥5. df≤0 is rejected.

rows.implemented: Editable preset-sized tables, margins/E/contributions/df, low-E gate and meaningful whole-row/column merges.
rows.limit: Requires sampling/model assumptions; asymptotic law is approximate. No arbitrary dimension editor or Yates correction.

rows.implemented: Average ranks/ties; official-table method, tail mapping, signed direction,4dp boundary and conditions.
rows.limit: Verified subset of official rows/cells only. Ties descriptive; no ordinary no-ties table inference. Table threshold does not supply an exact observed p-value.

enrichment.meaning: Fixed parameter, random intervals; finite observed coverage versus nominal. A teaching realization of CI interpretation.

enrichment.topic: Exact ordered enumeration and sample provenance
enrichment.meaning: Weighted possible samples and expectation contributions; teaching support, not an additional exam technique.

enrichment.topic: TypeI/II, power, p-values and conditional randomization
enrichment.meaning: Explanatory enrichment requested by the user; not explicitly named specification clauses. Each method/null is separately labelled.
Complete fictional frame permits exact design spread. This is not SE estimated from one sample and is supplementary support.
Average ranks are descriptive. Specification expects understanding ties but excludes numerical examination questions with ties.
